B18.capture_spec: C18-eight-reads: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C18-eight-reads.json, 8.8 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The square sprite at thickness 3: with the four sides only, the corners of the line stay empty; as the voice says 'the four corners' the eight reads (07-eight-reads) switch on and the corners fill in. Verified: on the square sprite at thickness 3 the eight reads add exactly 576 canvas px (4 x 3 x 3 x 16) to the four-read line, the corner holes (analyze_scenes C18); same picture as the loop (analyze_lab A6: 0 pixels differ at thickness 1, 2, 3, 4, 8)
B18.visual_intent: Act title 'Say It with a Loop' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left: the eight-read shader (14 lines); the first two lines of reads are marked, then the two lines of corner reads, then all four read lines together. At right a real Godot window with the square sprite: with the four sides only, the corners of its line stay empty; as the voice says 'the four corners' they fill in and the frame is complete.
B18.motion_claim: Focus lands on the side reads, then the corner reads, and the empty corners of the line fill in; then all eight reads at once.

show.event: corner reads; the empty corners fill in

B18.runner_up: manim: eight arrows around a cell
B18.why: The corners filling in as the corner reads are named: the code's effect on the real picture, and the thing the next beat replaces.

B19.capture_spec: C19-loop: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C19-loop.json, still PNG, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. 08-loop at thickness 3 on the square sprite: the same complete frame the eight written-out reads drew. Verified: draws the same picture as the eight written-out reads: 0 pixels differ from the last frame of the previous capture (analyze_scenes C19; analyze_lab A6)
B19.visual_intent: Code card at left: the loop shader (14 lines); focus lands on the outer for, the inner for, the line that reads and adds, then the loop as a whole. At right the same complete frame on the square sprite, unchanged by rewriting the reads as a loop. A caption carries one plain line for 'for'.
B19.motion_claim: Focus steps into the loop: outer for, inner for, the read.
B19.why: Paced line focus on the real code with its real result beside it.

B20.visual_intent: A 3 by 3 block of outline cells with offsets (-1,-1) to (1,1) written small in each cell and a terracotta center cell labelled 'me'. The nine cells light in loop order, row by row, and a '9 offsets' count ticks up. Beside it the one-line code 'vec2(float(x), float(y))' with the labels 'float: a decimal number' and 'vec2: a bundle of two numbers' on it, and under it a plain-shell box with the message the Shader Lab printed ('SHADER ERROR:' is the Lab's own prefix, the rest is the engine's text): SHADER ERROR: Invalid arguments for the built-in function: "vec2(int,int)".
B20.motion_claim: The nine cells light one after another in loop order and the middle one is marked as the pixel itself.

show.event: block, nine cells light, middle marked

B20.why: A grid lighting in loop order is the loop; the real compiler text is shown as a boxed artifact inside it.

B21.capture_spec: C21-same-picture: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C21-same-picture.json, 11.2 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. Left eight written-out reads, right the loop; thickness 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 as the voice counts; zero pixels differ at every step. Verified: 0 pixels differ at thickness 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8, hard-edged sprite (analyze_lab A6; scene C21 frames)
B21.visual_intent: Two real sprites side by side, the eight-read shader on the left and the loop on the right, their lines growing together through thickness one, two, three, four and eight; the two pictures stay identical at every step. Labels under each; at the end the readout '0 pixels differ'.
B21.motion_claim: Both rings grow in lockstep and stay identical.
B21.why: Watching two real pictures stay identical through the sweep is the evidence; a table of zeros is only the summary.

B22.visual_intent: A horizontal bar chart on the cream stage: four bars grow left to right for a 3 by 3, 5 by 5, 7 by 7 and 9 by 9 block (10, 26, 50 and 82 reads per pixel), labelled with the measured milliseconds per frame (10, 24, 44 and 71, the whole-millisecond medians of the valid runs); a thin dashed floor line at 7.5 ms is labelled 'no shader'. A small grey credit: 'stress test: 403 million pixels a frame · Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · wall-clock, vsync off, median of runs · the card's own timer unreadable'. A last small caption: 'a 300 x 300 sprite: 90,000 pixels'.
B22.motion_claim: The bars grow in turn, each longer than the last, as the read count goes up.

show.event: the 9 by 9 bar (82 reads), the longest; credit line

B22.why: Bars growing with the read count show 'time follows reads'; a table would only list the numbers.

B23.visual_intent: A code card (monospace, 17 lines) of the guard shader with the line 'if (thickness > 0.0) {' and its closing brace highlighted. Beside it a small pixel grid where every cell follows the same arrow: with thickness 0 all cells go to 'skip: one read'; a switch flips to thickness 2 and all cells go to 'read ten'. Under the card a plain-shell box with the message the Shader Lab printed ('SHADER ERROR:' is the Lab's own prefix, the rest is the engine's text): SHADER ERROR: Using 'return' in the 'fragment' processor function is incorrect.
B23.motion_claim: One switch flips and every cell changes its arrow together; the loop lines dim when the guard is false.

show.event: all cells to 'skip'; loop lines dim

B23.why: The idea is one switch everyone obeys; a grid of cells taking the same arrow shows it where a render cannot.

B24.visual_intent: Two pixel grids side by side. Left, titled 'per-pixel test': cells are split in two colors along the sprite's edge and the boundary cells hold different arrows (they disagree) and are ringed in terracotta. Right, titled 'thickness > 0.0': every cell holds the same arrow (they agree). Grey attribution under the left grid: 'GPU Gems 2, chapter 34, 2005'. Grey line under the right: 'shading language docs: no warning for if'.
B24.motion_claim: Arrows appear in each cell; on the left the edge cells point two ways, on the right every arrow is the same.

show.event: right grid: all arrows the same

B24.why: Disagreeing neighbors against agreeing ones is a picture of the idea; the quotes are the captions.

Labels 'no guard' and 'guard', one ring round the left sprite's rim, readout '224 pixels'.
B25.motion_claim: Both rings switch off; one sprite is clean, the other still has a tinted rim.

show.event: labels; both rings go to zero

B25.runner_up: manim: pixel row of the rim with alpha values
B25.why: Two real sprites at thickness zero, one clean and one tinted, is the evidence; the count is the readout.

B26.capture_spec: C26-select: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C26-select.json, 13.3 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. The script on screen sets thickness 0 in _ready; a scripted key press selects (thickness 2) as the voice says 'selected', another deselects on 'not'. Verified: 0 outline px before, 632 after the first key, 0 after the second; thickness reads back 0.0 (verify_j J1)
B26.visual_intent: Code card at left: the 11-line GDScript (a selected flag, _ready setting thickness 0, a key handler that sets 2 or 0); at right the real Godot window running it: no line, then a scripted key press at the word 'selected' draws the outline, a second press removes it. A label 'scripted input' stays on screen.
B26.motion_claim: The key handler lights up and the line around the sprite appears and disappears with each press.
B26.why: Cause (one call) and effect (the line) together; the script is the exact text that was run.

props.caption: instance uniform: its own value on each node that shares the material

B27.capture_spec: C27-shared-material: scene spec evidence/planning-checks/scenes/C27-shared-material.json, 14.3 s clip (stretched to the measured audio), 30 fps, 1280x720 canvas rendered at 3840x2160, Forward+, nearest filter. Two units share one material. Until the voice says 'instance' the dial is an ordinary uniform: setting thickness 2 on the left outlines both. After it, an instance uniform: left 2, right 0, one material, one ring. Verified: shared material: setting 3 on one unit draws 960 px on it and 960 px on the other; instance uniform on a shared material: 960 px on one, the other keeps its own value (verify_j J2, J3)
B27.visual_intent: Two real units side by side that share one material. The dial is set on the left unit and BOTH light up (readout 'both lit'); then the shader declares the uniform as instance, each node gets its own value, and only the left unit stays lit (readout 'one lit'). A caption gives the film's definition of an instance uniform (the series' wording).
B27.motion_claim: One unit is selected and both light up; after the fix, one unit is selected and only it lights up.

show.event: the shader switches to the instance uniform; only the left ring stays

B27.runner_up: manim: two boxes pointing at one material
B27.why: The real surprise (two nodes, one dial) and its real cure, in one clip.
